# US Liquidity and Treasury Market Deep Dive Analysis

Report 100 | Published 2022-12-26 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2022-12-26/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/100.json)

Liquidity caution and short-duration income.

The short-Treasury cash-parking thesis worked within its first-half horizon, and office-refinancing stress was well diagnosed. The Q1 net-liquidity decline, flat TGA, 2023 recession, gold-over-stocks and delayed Bitcoin recovery calls failed. Long-horizon Bitcoin direction succeeded. BOJ outcomes undermine claims that high debt makes permanent YCC mathematically unavoidable. Several retrospective successes repeat earlier forecasts and must not inflate a hit rate.

**Coverage:** All article text blocks were read. Ledger covers material macro, investment, and causal propositions; incidental descriptive statistics, boilerplate, and unreasoned position lists are excluded. Image labels were read, not image pixels.

## Claims

### 100-C01

**Dollar weakness eases debt**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Right |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | dollar-global-debt-liquidity |
| Source blocks | 8, 10, 24, 25, 42 |
| Thesis family | dollar-global-debt-liquidity |

A weaker dollar reduces local-currency servicing costs for unhedged dollar liabilities. Trade receipts, hedging and dollar assets change country exposure; the mechanism alone does not determine global GDP.

**Direction:** Supported within the defined test.

**Timing:** No numerical deadline was stated.

**Mechanism:** See rationale; this is not a forecast hit.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [Global liquidity: a new phase?](https://www.bis.org/publications/qr-202312/global-liquidity-new-phase) | BIS | 2023-12-04 | Verified in the audit

Dollar-credit growth turned from +6% in Q3 2021 to -4% at end-2022; EME dollar credit fell 5% year-on-year by mid-2023, coinciding with stronger USD and tighter policy.

- [Global liquidity at September 2021](https://www.bis.org/publications/202201-commentary-ibs-gli) | BIS | Verified in the audit

Dollar credit outside the US stood at $13.4tn, including $4.2tn to emerging/developing borrowers. Currency denomination differs from lender nationality.

### 100-C22

**Q1 liquidity decline**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Wrong |
| Type | forecast |
| Horizon | Q1 2023 |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | 2023-q1-net-liquidity-decline |
| Source blocks | 123, 126, 140, 142 |
| Thesis family | 2023-q1-net-liquidity-decline |

Applying the article formula on matched Wednesdays gives $5,830.240 billion on December 28 and $6,257.503 billion on March 29, an increase of $427.263 billion. Bank emergency lending and TGA drawdown outweighed ongoing securities runoff. This is a direct test of the stated indicator, not an equity-correlation inference.

**Direction:** Contradicted within the defined test.

**Timing:** Assessed against the stated horizon: Q1 2023

**Mechanism:** A matching outcome alone does not establish causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [WALCL](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/WALCL) | Original agency via FRED | 2026-11-07 | Verified in the audit

Same-Wednesday Fed assets minus TGA minus daily ON RRP: December 28, 2022 $5,830.240 billion; March 29, 2023 $6,257.503 billion, an increase of $427.263 billion. WALCL and WTREGEN millions; RRPONTSYD billions multiplied by 1,000.

## Framework lessons

- Match debt maturities to policy lags.

## Verification limitations

- Captured website text is not an authenticated publication-date version.
- Chart-only numerical claims have not been visually verified.
- Selected stock/ETF adjusted-close comparisons are disclosed where used; no reconstructed portfolio backtest has been performed.
- Unresolved verdicts are not forecast failures or successes; no aggregate hit rate is inferred.
- Block 138 describes year-end TGA as achieved in a report dated December 26, before quarter-end; this could be premature wording or a later edit. The snapshot cannot establish which.
